newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican police paid witch who planted body - gov't.
newsitem.headline: Mexican police paid witch who planted body - gov't.

text.p: A former top Mexican law official paid some $500,000 to a reputed witch and her friends who allegedly planted a body in the ranch of ex-president Carlos Salinas' brother Raul, authorities charged on Tuesday.

In the latest twist to a soap opera-like drama that has gripped the nation, Mexico City Attorney General Jose Antonio Gonzalez said the man in charge of investigating Raul Salinas on murder charges paid money to people suspected of rigging evidence against the ex-president's brother.

He said Pablo Chapa Bezanilla, ex-special prosecutor at the attorney general's office, paid one million pesos ($130,000) in government funds to the witch, known as La Paca, two days before the buried body was discovered last October.
Another man allegedly involved in the planting of the body received 2.5 million pesos ($330,000), he added.
When the body was discovered last October, authorities suggested it belonged to a congressman suspected of taking part in the murder of one of the leaders of Mexico's ruling party in Sept. 1994.
Raul Salinas is in jail on charges of masterminding that murder. The congressmen dissappeared more than two years ago.
In fact, authorities said, the body was not that of the congressman, but was a dead relative of La Paca, who was dug up from his grave and re-buried at Salinas' ranch on the outskirts of Mexico City.
La Paca, whose real name is Francisca Zetina, is already in jail along with eight accomplices on grave robbing and other charges.
Raul has denied responsibility in the murder case, and the discovery of the planted body appeared to bolster his chances of acquittal. He also faces illicit enrichment charges.
Chapa, until he was fired in December, was in charge of the case against Raul Salinas.
Gonzalez said Chapa used attorney general's office funds to make the payments, but he did not speculate whether they were bribed to plant the body, or whether the payments were made as a reward.
He said Chapa had failed to respond to a summons to testify on his role regarding the discovery of the body. Press reports have suggested he was on the run.

Chapa's former boss, ex-Attorney General Antonio Lozano, late on Tuesday issued a communique saying he was prepared to testify on his role in the case, and he suggested political interests were at work in discrediting him and his team.
"I'm sure that once beyond the electoral interests...my public conduct and that of my collaborators will be justly valued by society," he said, referring to mid-term elections in July.

Lozano was the only member of an opposition party in the cabinet, and he rocked the country by arresting powerful figures like Raul Salinas, a prominent member of the Institutional Revolutionary Party that has ruled for 67 years.
Like Chapa, Lozano was fired last December after the Salinas case appeared to be unravelling.
